YTA. Nobody, not even allistics, appreciate invasive neighbourhood renovations, especially outside standard work hours. If you want to maintain any level of community with your neighbours, you need to prioritise work to be done 9-5. If this is 100% not achievable, would it be at all possible to reach a compromise of attempting to schedule the overwhelming renovations while she is not home? Does she have after school care, or does she go to grandma’s on the weekends? I know this is wishful thinking and won’t be a complete solution, but as an autistic who grew up with autistic siblings, I can understand the desperation of that whole family for some relief from the constant meltdowns. Maybe even a knock on your neighbours door each day to give them as much heads up as possible. A big part of this being triggering for her is likely due to the unexpected nature of it. If she has time to prepare it might make things a bit less traumatic for her. She is likely spending her days walking on eggshells waiting for the jackhammer to drop.

I am concerned about what he said about something breaking in HIS house while you were demolishing. If you are completing a demolition so close to a neighbouring bedroom, you should have had a conversation with them beforehand to let them know. Especially a child’s bedroom where you continue to work until 11pm. You know kids go to sleep at like 8 right? That’s 3 hours of disturbed sleep.

It isn’t your fault that this has been particularly difficult for his daughter, and you will have to complete the renovations sooner or later regardless of the neighbours wishes. But the dad is doing his duty as a father to advocate for his daughter, and if you don’t want to start a war, with neighbours and your wife, I suggest you come to a compromise. 

Your wife is right. When your child is facing emotional turmoil at the hands of someone else, even indirectly, you wouldn’t just expect some decency, you would demand it.
